items.stem: Reserves are held by an insurer primarily to:

options.text: Ensure funds are available to pay future claims already incurred or expected
options.rationale: Correct: reserves back future claim obligations.

options.text: Record the insurer's profit for the year
options.rationale: Reserves are liabilities for future claims, not profit.
Reserves are for claims, not bonuses.
Premiums fund reserves; they are not replaced by them.

items.explanation: Correct: reserves back future claim obligations.

items.stem: Which two statements about pricing an insurance risk are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Expected claim cost is a key input to the premium
options.rationale: Correct: the expected cost of claims drives pricing.

options.text: Variability around the average also matters
options.rationale: Correct: uncertainty, not just the mean, affects pricing and capital.

options.text: Only the single most likely outcome matters
options.rationale: The full distribution matters, not one point.

options.text: Premiums should ignore the time value of money
options.rationale: Discounting of future cash flows is relevant.

items.explanation: Correct: the expected cost of claims drives pricing.
